div.p: Real-time tasks can be classified into three categories, based on the "seriousness" of deadline misses -hard, soft and weakly hard real-time tasks. The consequences of a deadline miss of a hard real-time task cannot be accepted whereas soft real-time tasks tolerate "some" deadline misses. While, in a weakly hard real-time task, the distribution of its met and missed deadlines is stated and specified precisely. Due to the complexity and significantly increased functionality in system computation, attention has been given to multiprocessor scheduling, comprised of several processors. Due to the fact that in multiprocessor, there have more than one processor, algorithms which can cater higher computational complexity for task allocation and for task migration are highly required. Thus, the sufficient and efficient scheduling algorithm supported by accurate schedulability analysis technique is presented to provide weakly hard real-time guarantees. In this paper, a schedulability analysis to schedule weakly hard real-time tasks has been proposed by using the global multiprocessor scheduling technique, called multiprocessor response time analysis combining with the exact analysis, named hyperperiod analysis and deadline models; weakly hard constraints and ~-pattern under static priority scheduling. Then, the Matlab simulation tool is used in order to validate the result of analysis. From the performance evaluation results, it proved that the proposed approach is satisfied the tasks deadlines with less number of misses.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Scheduling theory is the theoretical foundation for proving the correctness of real-time systems [1]. Thus, many scheduling theories have been developed to predict the timing behaviour of the task set. A scheduling algorithm determines when to execute which task on which processor if it has more than one processor. By far, several scheduling algorithms with different condition have been designed in order to analyse a system.

Therefore, schedulability analysis is used as verification whether each task in task sets provided will be meet a deadline when scheduled based on which scheduling algorithm/scheme that adopted. Schedulability analysis can be used at design 978-1-4673-8227-4/15/$31.00 ©2015 IEEE 123 time or at run time. The advantage of schedule at design time is to ensure the systems would be correctly functioning before execution in order to avoid system failure. Meanwhile, ifusing at run time, a task can be determined whether it should be admitted or not to the system during execution.

Real-time systems or tasks are divided into three classes, based on the importance of deadline misses -hard real-time tasks, soft real-time tasks and weakly hard real-time tasks [2]. The consequences of deadlines miss for a hard real-time task system cannot be tolerated because some failure can affects the systems performance whereas " some" deadline misses are tolerated for soft real-time task systems. Usually, hard tasks co-exist with soft tasks; thus, it means that most hard real-time tasks are not that hard actually. It may happen that the application of real-time consists ofa mix of hard and soft realtime tasks, and it called weakly hard real-time system. Avionics can be an example of systems with weakly hard real-time requirements because some delay during execution is acceptable in that system and it is unnecessary to meet all the tasks deadlines as long as the misses are specified precisely. The cases analysed by Bernat [1] show that some systems, such as an automatic control system, do not act as truly hard systems since the algorithm itself could tolerate missed deadlines to a certain degree.

In this paper, weakly hard real-time tasks have been studied rather than hard and soft real-time tasks because "weakly hard" precisely define and specify the distribution of missed and met deadlines for the tasks during a given time period.

In the past, much of research efforts have been focused on scheduling and schedulability analysis of uniprocessor system, as well as in weakly hard real-time scheduling. This is because, the complexion of scheduling in multiprocessor systems is more than in uniprocessor system because it is not solved by applying straightforward extensions of techniques. In contrast, a complete theory of weakly hard real-time scheduling for multiprocessor systems is still to come. Hence, as a challenge, this paper deals with weakly hard real-time scheduling with many processors, called multiprocessor.

Multiprocessor scheduling can be classified as either partitioned or global (or some combination thereof, called hybrid) [3]. In partitioning scheduling, each task is allocated to a specific processor permanently or in other words. an execution of the task is permitted only on that processor with no migration and each processor independently schedules its assigned tasks using a uniprocessor scheduling algorithm. And, in the partitioning multiprocessor scheduling, usually, divided a task set into groups beforehand. Then, a separate ready queue holds by each processor such that a specific processor is assigned by each task group. In global scheduling, task preemptions and migrations are permitted, that is a task preempted on a particular processor may resume execution on the same or on a different processor. Additionally, in global multiprocessor scheduling, need to allocate the available processors to the highest priority task in the ready queue.

For example, applications of modern embedded used in multimedia devices, automatic control systems, robotics and safety critical systems, are often executed on multiprocessor systems. The objective of this paper is to provide a schedulability analysis of periodic and preemptive weakly hard real-time tasks on multiprocessor systems when global scheduling approach is adopted. Static scheduling takes attention because it is an attractive option for applications of real-time since both the predictability of high resource utilization and worst case behaviour can be ensure by it. This is because task will miss deadlines in predictable way and the number of preemptions is bounded. A static priority scheduling algorithm is often implemented in scheduling systems because this scheme is relatively easy to implement and requires less overhead than dynamic schemes because it does not change over time. This paper aims to contribute towards guaranteed and satisfied weakly hard real-time scheduling and can forecast the implementation of the task, with less task migrations and less number of deadlines miss.

The paper is then structured as follows: Section IT presents the related works. Then, the weakly hard scheduling approach is placed in Section TTT. After that, cruise control with collision avoidance system case study is in Section TV. Section V discusses a schedulability analysis in global scheduling. Performance evaluation is present in Section VI. Tn Section VIT, some conclusions are discussed and remaining an ongoing work.

div.head: IT. RELATED WORKS
div.p: There have been some efforts to schedule weakly hard real-time tasks on multiprocessor systems. Wu and Jin proposed the classical weakly hard real-time scheduling algorithms, namely Distance Based Priority (DBP), which originally was introduced by [4] on uniprocessor system. to apply into multiprocessor applications to guarantee QoS of both hard real-time tasks and multimedia streams even under overload conditions [5]. However, MPDBPs cannot maximize the performance and satisfaction ratio of the task deadline when the system is under loaded or even when possible, and consequently, the quality of service for applications of multimedia streaming is ultimately fails to be good as provided.

Another work is done by Kong and Cho [6] wherein they proposed the first dynamic real-time scheduling algorithm for 124 (m,k)-firm deadline constrained tasks on homogenous multiprocessors to guarantee the performance of algorithm, called the Guaranteed Multiprocessor Real-Time Scheduling (GMRTS-MK) algorithm. However, the algorithm that they use will cause an increase in the ratio caused by the increasing number of tasks. Later, the same author, Kong and Cho [7] introduced an Energy-constrained Multiprocessor Real-Time Scheduling (EMRTS-MK) class algorithms for weakly hard real-time for (m,k)-firm deadline constrained tasks running on multiprocessor.

Several static and dynamic approaches on global multiprocessor scheduling have been proposed but most prior research is limits for hard and soft real-time tasks. The most well-known static priority scheduling algorithm is hybrid priority assignment like Rate Monotonic with Utilization Separation (RM-US) [8], that obtain much better scheduling performances and scheduling the remaining ones with RMA. Thereafter, Pathan and Jonsson [9] proposed a priority assignment for global fixed priority scheduling, called the Fixed-Priority Test (FPT) test. Later, Back et aI, [10] presented a new schedulability analysis approach, called the Earliest-Quasi-Deadline-First (EQDF) algorithm. EQDF assigns priority to jobs according to their quasi-deadlines.

Bertogna and Cirinei [II] adapted response time analysis by iteratively computing an upper bound on the response time of each task. Further, Guan et aI, rl2l extended the response time analysis of rIll. Sun et al. rl3l address the problem of schedulability analysis for a set of sporadic tasks with arbitrary deadlines running on a multiprocessor system with global fixed-priority preemptive scheduling.

Proportionate-fair (Pfair) [14], which uses a quantum based model is known as an optimal scheduling algorithm for global scheduling. However, this algorithm will generate a number of task preemptions and migration overhead and it is very complex to implement. There are some simple dynamic priority scheduling algorithm which perform fairly well with a small number of task preemptions and migration overhead, such as Earliest Deadline First with Utilization Separation (EDF-US). But, much better in order to achieve performances of scheduling for multiprocessor systems is Earliest Deadline until Zero Laxity (EDZL) [IS]. Nevertheless, their utilization bounds for schedulable systems are just 50%.

Based on the review, research efforts on scheduling weakly hard real-time tasks on multiprocessor are relatively promising area of research. Previous works have investigated how to predict the temporal behaviour and to determine whether the timing requirements of an application tasks will be met. However, many of their works are extremely applied on hard real-time tasks. Studies have shown that some researchers has adopted the approach of using response time analysis in global scheduling. But, it is limited to sporadic tasksets. Hence, this paper finds a solution to schedule periodic weakly hard real-time tasks by applying multiprocessor response time analysis.

div.head: ITI. THE WEAKLY HARD SCHEDULING APPROACH
div.p: The main focused of research on multiprocessor scheduling is on guaranteeing the completion of deadlines.

However, for weakly hard real-time tasks where violation of a task is allowed, we proposed the weakly hard scheduling approach to cater task migration problem in global scheduling. In this approach, we used well-known and a useful performance metric, response time analysis scheduled with fixed priority. Within the context of preemptive scheduling of periodic tasksets, in order to make the multiprocessor scheduling algorithm resilient with exceptions, the algorithms must be combined with specific techniques such as hyperperiod analysis first to recover from deadline missing. Deadline models or temporal constraints of weakly hard models that derived from [1] are used for schedulability analysis. The weakly hard constraints and Il-pattern that used for weakly hard real-time tasks are to guarantee that a tolerance for deadline misses limited to a specified upper bound that can be satisfied. Fig. 1 depicted the flow chart of the proposed weakly hard scheduling approach. Tn the following sub-section, the details for each of the approaches stated in the figure will be explained.

div.head: A. Global Scheduling Algorithm
div.p: Tn the global approach [3], migration is allowed; where during execution, migration of the tasks among processors is permitted arbitrarily. There have two level of migration for global scheduling based on the allowed migration degree. Job level migration means each job of a task can be run on any processor. But a job started on a given processor cannot be moved on another. Task level migration where a task can run at any time on any processor.
The advantages of using global scheduling algorithms, tasks are dynamically assigned to the processing units which available and it can succeed in meeting deadlines.

div.head: C. Hyperperiod Analysis
div.p: Another alternative to study the performance of a scheduling algorithm, or to verity the schedulability of a task set, is through the use of an exact analysis such as hyperperiod analysis. Similarly, it can be used to verity if a task set misses any deadline, showing if it is unschedulable. Also, it can be used as a sufficient condition for unschedulability. The task set hyperperiod (0, H(T » is a feasibility interval for implicit and constrained deadline synchronous periodic tasksets, when scheduled by a deterministic and memoryless algorithm, such as RMA [17]. For these algorithms, the schedulability of the task set can be verified by checking if the schedule generated misses any deadline using the least common multiple calculation. It is possible to use hyperperiod analysis on multiprocessor scheduling because of using periodic task with deadline and preemptive fixed priority scheduling.

div.head: D. Weakly hard constraints and j1-pattern
div.p: Bernat et al. [1] defmed the weakly hard constraints in order to precisely specifY how many deadlines may be missed and met. The consecutiveness of lost deadlines is very sensitive for some systems while others are only sensitive to the number of deadlines missed. The merge of the two judgments, (a) consecutiveness vs. non-consecutiveness, and (b) missed vs. met deadlines concretely guides to four basic constraints (n 2: 1, n::; m).

A Il-pattern is a pattern of deadlines missed during a period of time. A Il-pattern is denoted by a 0 (zeros) that represent missed deadlines and by a 1 (ones) represent met deadlines. The sequence of zeros and ones can be used to characterise a task. div.head: IV. A CRUISE CONTROL WITH COLLISION A VOIDANCE (CCCA) SYSTEM CASE STUDY
div.p: We chose the CCCA case study based on the one described by [18] because it consists of hard and soft tasks. Thus, it is unnecessary for the system meeting all of task deadlines, but the misses must be specified precisely. We first present a task set that was derived from the CCCA system, which consist of four tasks.

The four main subsystems of the CCCA used in the case study consist of Braking Control (BC), Engine Control (EC), Collision Avoidance (CA) and Display Control (DC). Each subsystems has deadline that equals its period. The CCCA system used in modern vehicles is to assist the driver in maintaining the speed of vehicle and maintaining a safe distance to other vehicles.

The goal of CCCA system is to increase efficiency of modern vehicles. Among the four tasks, two tasks, that is the Braking Control and Collision Avoidance tasks are specified as hard periodic tasks. Meanwhile, another two tasks, the Engine Control and Display Control tasks are specified as soft periodic tasks.

div.head: V. A SCHEDULABILITY ANALYSIS IN GLOBAL SCHEDULING
div.p: A condition to know whether a task set meets its deadlines or not is a schedulability tests or analysis. The system behaves in global scheduling as explained in details as follows. The processor is assigned with each task in order to assign a local (for a processor) with static priority. In a multiprocessor system, an upper bound of the response time of a task 1"i scheduled with fixed priority can be derived by the fixed point iteration on the value R j, starting with Rj = Cj. Braking Control has the highest priority among the four tasks, thus it selected as the first task to assign to Processor 1. From the interference defmition, it is clear that no task can contribute to the interference on a higher priority task.

Consider the four tasks in Table I, where these tasks needed to be scheduled using 2 processors with response time analysis technique. It also shows which processor of each task is assigned. Later, a timing diagram which has been designed for a global scheduling algorithm along with the worst case response time is illustrate in Fig. 2. From the figure, task Display Control missed its deadline by five time units. This is because; task Display Control only finished its execution 20 time units from its total time units, 25. This is made task Display Control unschedulable. Nevertheless, hyperperiod analysis and weakly hard deadline models/temporal constraints can be used to guarantee that both deadlines and constraints are satisfied ifthere have one or more tasks missed its deadline. In order to guarantee that task Display Control meet its deadlines (by defined the exact number of deadlines can be missed) and satisfy its weakly hard temporal constraints, then, an exact analysis is perform to make the tasks predictable and schedulable.

As can be seen from the result in Table IT, by using hyperperiod analysis, even though task Display Control missed its deadline in the worst case, the number of missed deadlines can be specified for that task.

The Fig. 3 shows the worst case response time at each invocation within the hyperperiod at priority level 4. Each vertical line represents the worst case response time of the task. The deadline ofthe task is D4 = 50. The hyperperiod h4 = 150. This means that the task is invoked <4 = 3 times within its hyperperiod at level 4. The following Table III shows the exact distribution ofthe missed and met deadlines for invocations 1 to 150 of task Display Control. A 0 represents a deadline missed and a 1 a deadline met. It can miss 3 times every 150 invocations during its hyperperiod. Hence, (2,3) constraint is defined of the weakly hard constraint for task Display Control. We can concluded that the system is weakly hard schedulable eventhough task Display Control miss its deadline, it is satisfied the weakly hard constraint.

div.head: VI. PERFORMANCE EV ALUA nON
div.p: In this section, we give the autonomous mobile robot (AMR) case study derived from [19] as benchmark. We applied the task set of AMR into our experiment and the results are shown in Table TV. IV, the reader should realize that task Subsumption missed its deadline in the worst case. This is because the response time, Ri for that task is exceeded the deadline. However, in the hyperperiod at level 4, the number of invocations of a task, ai illustrate that it can miss 2 times every 100 invocations during its hyperperiod.

As a comparison with the result in [20], the Fig. 4 show the distribution of task Subsumption based on hyperperiod analysis for 10 invocations. The deadline of the task is D~ = 50. The task misses at one deadline in every 10 invocations. There are two performances that can be highlighted in this paper. Firstly, as shown in this section, from the result of performance evaluation, task Subsumption missed its deadline using multiprocessor response time analysis while task manrobotinifmissed its deadline when it is scheduled by using R-BOUND-MP-NFRNS in the previous paper. Secondly, based on the result as depicted in Fig 4 ., AMR case study on global scheduling has better performance of schedulability tests compared to partitioned scheduling in terms of achieves a higher success/meet ratio when there is some deadlines missed for the task. This is due to the fact that the number of invocations for the task of AMR when using global scheduling approach is lesser than partitioned scheduling approach. This is proved that the greater value of meet/success ratio an approach has the better performance of schedulability the approach is.

div.head: VIT. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: As conclusion, in this paper, we presented a schedulability analysis by proposing a multiprocessor scheduling approach to schedule periodic weakly hard real-time task. Firstly, we use multiprocessor response time analysis as a technique to derive schedulability tests of task. Then, we analysed the task using hyperperiod analysis and weakly hard deadline models/temporal constraints in order to precisely specity the number of deadline met and missed. Our experimental simulation validates that the proposed approach achieves our objective/aim and provide a solution to the problem stated in this paper.

Regarding this approach, wherein, we proposed schedulability analysis approach for global multiprocessor scheduling that consists of an efficient scheduling technique, named RTA and weakly hard models. Hence, it can be used by designers to build real-time systems for which predictability and adaptability are key points. For future work, we aim to combine elements of both partitioned and global scheduling in order to schedule weakly hard real-time tasks.
